_note: Administration zone. A building with a 'fixed' block is part of the Shaft as built: the player cannot place, move or remove it, and the opening layout places it once on the level it names. Everything else here is placed by the player. These buildings mostly enable political capability rather than producing anything — which is why they are the first thing a player under resource pressure wants to cut, and why cutting them is a trap. The archive gates the Apocrypha, and therefore the whole Chapter 2 mechanic.

buildings.name: Council chamber
buildings._note: Its repair cost is timber for chamber fittings — the ceremonial spend that buys legitimacy. Let it decay and the Accord cannot be amended at all.

buildings.name: Archive
buildings._note: Holds the Apocrypha in its restricted rear chamber, and therefore the Nexus. Also where Chapter 1's archive-record inconsistencies are found. Neglecting the archive quietly closes the story down.

buildings.name: Judicial chamber
buildings._note: Both halves of the law in one room: the Accord is amended at the bench and applied to a person in the dock. Keeping it out of the council chamber is what lets a player have law without courts, or courts that outlive the council whose statutes they apply.

buildings.name: The Exit
buildings._note: The only door onto the outside, and the only building here the player did not choose: it was there before them and cannot be moved or taken down. Four slots, so it and the auditorium fill level 1 exactly: a cell with a bench where somebody who has asked to leave spends their last day, a bay where they are suited up in a full-body suit, and two slots of the door itself.

buildings.name: Security post
buildings._note: The Order faction's physical footprint. Every one built trades freedom for stability at a fixed rate, which is the whole game in one building.

buildings.name: Holding cells
buildings._note: Unlocks the harsh branch of several dilemmas. Without it, 'make an example of him' is not on the menu — the buildings a player owns shape which rulings they are even offered.
